title: The memory contract: one item, the order a reader sees, the brief under a budget
request: The owner: continue the memory plan non-stop after 35.0 (the embedding test waits for the models to be pulled); 35.1 is the contract every agent's memory shares.
spec: MEMORY_PLAN.md 35.1: dclab_core/memory.py with MemoryItem v1 and Brief v1; check (one line, length, a source, no protected name); resolve (scope order, corrections first); select (the brief under a token budget, deterministic). Done when an item without a source, with two lines or naming a protected column is refused, a correction beats what it corrects, a narrower scope beats a wider one, the same items give the same brief, and the wheel check passes.
plan: Read the core's contract conventions and the existing playbook and screen (Phase 9's H2), to reuse rather than duplicate.
Write the tests first: the item's rules, the reader's order, the brief, counters, the host's row.
Write dclab_core/memory.py, register it, generate the schemas, add the host row adapter and the integration section.
Review adversarially, fix every finding with a test, then the version bump, the wheel check, the record and the commit.

decisions.decision: memory.named is a general copy of the challenge packs' matching, with a test that the two agree
decisions.why: the plan said 35.1 builds the name filter once for H2, but H2's screen already existed on challenge_pack.names_in, a module the open edition leaves out; memory must stand in the open edition

decisions.decision: An item's id is the hash of its kind, scope and normalised words in any script, with the signs that change a meaning kept
decisions.why: the same words in the same scope are one item and a forged id is refused; Latin-only words would give every Persian item one id, and dropping signs merged 'tenure < 6' with 'tenure > 6'

decisions.decision: The main product's entry is 'library output' with the reason, and the row it would add lives in adapters/main_product_memory.py
decisions.why: the main product has no memory table at the commit its fields were read from; the registry accepts module:function only for rows that exist there

decisions.decision: A correction is a person's only; an agent's item may never hide a person's correction
decisions.why: the plan's rule that a person's correction wins at any scope; an agent's change of mind is a new item

decisions.decision: A retired item that was replaced (retired_by set) still hides what it corrected; one withdrawn (no retired_by) does not
decisions.why: a chain of corrections must keep the first wrong fact hidden, and withdrawing a correction must bring back what it replaced

decisions.decision: The version bump to 0.124.0 came after the H2 session committed 0.123.0
decisions.why: that session holds the core's version files uncommitted in the same folder; bumping first would be undone by its commit

change: dclab_core/memory.py (MemoryItem v1, Brief v1, item_id, named, check, resolve, select, cited, counted, retire), registered in contracts.py; adapters/main_product_memory.py (as_row, from_row); two entries in adapters/conformance.py; schemas and baselines; tests/test_core_memory.py (open edition) and tests/test_core_memory_host.py; a CORE_INTEGRATION.md section; the plan corrected where it said H2 was only planned.

findings.defect: The adapter registry had no entry for the two new contracts
findings.scenario: conformance.problems() listed memory_item and memory_brief as having no adapter and no reason, so test_conformance and make core-wheel-check failed
findings.cause: every contract needs an adapter or a reason, and the new ones had neither
findings.fix: both entries added as library output with the reason (no memory table in the main product; the row it would add named)

findings.defect: A one-line item could hold a second line or an invisible mark
findings.scenario: a text with a Unicode line separator passed; the brief's text then split into two lines, the second a bare instruction; bidi overrides and a text of one zero-width space passed too
findings.cause: the check refused control characters only, not line or paragraph separators or format marks
findings.fix: refuse control, line and paragraph separators and format marks except the two joiners Persian needs; require at least one word
findings.impact: a person's or a page's text could be stored as a line that reads as an instruction inside an agent's first message

findings.defect: Texts with opposite meanings got the same id
findings.scenario: 'tenure < 6 months is high risk' and 'tenure > 6 months is high risk' hashed alike, so the correction of a sign was refused as an item correcting itself
findings.fix: NFKC first, and the signs that change a meaning (comparison, equality, negation, percent, a minus before a number) kept as words
findings.impact: a person could not correct a wrong sign, and a store removing duplicates would merge contradicting facts

findings.defect: A retired copy of an item did not hide its active copy, and the input order chose between copies
findings.scenario: resolve([item, retire(item)]) still showed the item; two copies with different counters and the same time gave different results in the two input orders
findings.cause: the status was filtered before copies were merged, and copies were compared by time only
findings.fix: retired is final for its id; copies are ordered by time, counters and text, so the order never decides

findings.defect: An agent could hide a person's correction, an agent could mark its item a correction, and a cycle hid both items
findings.scenario: base, then the person's correction, then an agent's item superseding the correction: the reader saw only the agent's number; two items superseding each other both vanished
findings.cause: any active item's supersedes hid its target
findings.fix: a correction requires a person as its author; an item hides a correction only when it is one; edges forming a cycle hide nothing

findings.defect: The protected-name screen missed plurals, full-width letters and names in other scripts
findings.scenario: 'Group by order_ids.' and 'Group by OrderIDs.' passed the screen for order_id, the plan's own example of a leak in its plural
findings.cause: the matching was the challenge packs' one, which has the same gap, on ASCII words only
findings.fix: NFKC first, a plural of the last part and of capitals caught, letters of any script kept
findings.impact: a lesson carrying an evaluation's answer would have entered memory
findings.open: look-alike letters of another script are not caught; the challenge packs' own names_in still misses plurals (Phase 9's screen, not changed here)

findings.defect: Times were any string and sorted as text
findings.scenario: 'not a date' was accepted; 12:00+03:30 (08:30 UTC) sorted above 10:00 UTC
findings.cause: the field was a string of a length
findings.fix: an ISO time with its zone, stored as UTC

findings.defect: The brief could pass its budget by its line breaks
findings.scenario: ten short items under a budget of sixty gave a text one token over
findings.fix: the joined text is measured before a line is added

findings.defect: Retirement rules were loose, the host row refused a real timestamp, and the test file would not ship with the open edition
findings.scenario: an item retired by itself, a second retirement erasing the first's name, an active item with retired_by; a host's datetime column refused; the test file named a private dataset and imported closed modules
findings.cause: no validator for retired_by; from_row passed the column as it came; one test file held open and closed tests
findings.fix: retired_by only on a retired item and never itself; a second retirement keeps the name; from_row reads a datetime as ISO; the tests split into an open file and a host file, the private name replaced

outcome: The memory contract is built and reviewed: one item's rules, the reader's order with corrections that only a person makes, the brief under a budget counted on its whole text, and the host's row. Nine review findings fixed with tests, the two blocking ones being the missing registry entries and a hidden second line. Released as dclab-core 0.124.0, on top of the H2 session's 0.123.0.
lessons: A one-line rule must refuse every way Unicode ends a line or hides a mark, not only control characters; keep the joiners a script needs.
A normalisation for identity must keep what changes the meaning: signs and negation, not only words.
When corrections can chain, decide what a replaced correction and a withdrawn one each do, and test both.
Check what already exists before planning to build it: the plan said the name screen was to be built, and it was already there.
risks: Another session holds the core's version files uncommitted in the same folder.
A general name matcher can drift from the challenge packs' one; the agreement test only covers shared cases.
